research:
I couldn't open the Yahoo page, but news reports put the DAX at **25,415.06 at the close on 2026-09-14**. That is about 4.5% below its record high from late August. The question settles on the September 24 close (a Thursday) and nothing so far settles it.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the daily close of ^GDAXI on Yahoo Finance for 2026-09-24. That date is a Thursday and a normal Xetra trading day, so the fallback rule for weekends and holidays should not apply. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGDAXI/)
- I could not open the Yahoo history page (the connection was refused). Investing.com and boerse.de were blocked the same way, so the figures below come from news reports and search summaries.
- 2026-09-14: the DAX closed at 25,415.06 on Xetra, down 0.60%. It opened at 25,498.74, the day's high was 25,548.78 and the low was 25,325.52. The previous close was 25,568.56. Yahoo's ^GDAXI close normally matches the Xetra close. [finanzen.net](https://www.finanzen.net/nachricht/aktien/verluste-in-frankfurt-dax-schlussendlich-im-minus-15933409), [finanzen.ch](https://www.finanzen.ch/nachrichten/aktien/minuszeichen-in-frankfurt-dax-zum-handelsende-in-der-verlustzone-1036543606)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. There are 8 trading sessions from September 15 to 24.
- The current level of about 25,415 sits roughly in the middle of the question's range (23,500 to 28,000). It is about 1,900 points above the bottom and 2,600 below the top.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-14: SAP gained 5.08%, the best DAX stock. Hochtief fell 9.37%, Siemens Energy 8.04% and Infineon 7.72%. The MDAX fell 1.99%. A dpa-AFX weekly preview said the US rate decision would be a key marker for the "weakening" DAX and named oil above $100 and inflation worries as the main burdens. [finanzen.net](https://www.finanzen.net/nachricht/aktien/verluste-in-frankfurt-dax-schlussendlich-im-minus-15933409), [ariva](https://www.ariva.de/dax-index/news/wochenausblick-fuer-den-schwaechelnden-dax-wird-der-12134891)
- 2026-09-14: one preview said the DAX was starting a decisive rate week facing headwinds, with sharply rising oil prices. [ms-aktuell](https://ms-aktuell.de/?p=158277)
- 2026-09-11: the DAX closed at 25,568.56, up 0.82%. [ms-aktuell](https://ms-aktuell.de/?p=158277)
- 2026-09-10: the ECB raised all three key rates by 25 basis points, putting the deposit rate at 2.50%. This was its second hike of 2026, after June, and the reason given was higher inflation driven by energy prices from the Middle East war. The DAX fell about 0.7% to roughly 25,400 and dropped below 25,500 after the decision. [ms-aktuell](https://ms-aktuell.de/welt/ezb-zinsen-dax-10-09-2026/), [stock3](https://stock3.com/news/ezb-erhoeht-die-zinsen-dax-bricht-25-500-nasdaq-vor-29-000-17281005)
- 2026-09-07: the DAX opened the week below 26,000. Brent was moving toward $100 because Iran wanted to set up a demarcation zone around the Strait of Hormuz. [CMC Markets](https://www.cmcmarkets.com/en-gb/news-and-analysis/dax-starts-the-new-week-on-a-weak-note-as-oil-approaches-100-a-barrel)
- 2026-08-28: the DAX hit a record intraday high of 26,618.74 and closed at 26,569.99. [ms-aktuell](https://ms-aktuell.de/?p=154494)
- 2026-08-03: the DAX closed above 26,000 for the first time (26,001.31). By 2026-08-13 it had set 15 record highs this year. [stock3](https://stock3.com/news/dax-15-allzeithoch-in-2026-17239415)

## 4. Base rates
- Recent trend: the index fell about 4.5% from the August 28 record (about 26,570) to 25,415 on September 14. The pullback has come from oil and rising rates.
- My own rough estimate of how far the index might move in 8 trading days, not taken from a source:
  - If annualized volatility is around 15%, one standard deviation over 8 days is about 2.7%, or roughly ±680 points.
  - In a stressed market with volatility around 20%, it is about 3.6%, or roughly ±900 points.
- For context, recent single-day moves have been around 0.6% to 0.8%.
- Reaching either end of the question's range (-7.5% or +10%) within 8 sessions would take an unusually large move.
- September has historically been a weak month for the DAX. I did not find a source for the exact statistic.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket lists daily "DAX Up or Down" markets for September 2026. I did not find a market or price on the September 24 closing level. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/dax-up-or-down-on-september-30-2026)
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold markets and no expert point forecasts for this date.
- The 14 September previews were cautious and expected the DAX to struggle. [ariva](https://www.ariva.de/dax-index/news/wochenausblick-fuer-den-schwaechelnden-dax-wird-der-12134891)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-15/16: US Fed rate decision. The 14 September previews treated it as the key event of the week. [deltavalue](https://www.deltavalue.de/fed-zinsentscheid/)
- Week of September 14 to 18: other central bank meetings and Friday 2026-09-18, which is a quarterly options and futures expiry ("quad witching"). The expiry date is my inference from the usual third-Friday schedule. [Der Aktionär weekly radar](https://www.deraktionaer.de/artikel/maerkte-forex-zinsen/der-aktionaer-wochenausblick-14-bis-18-september-2026--20408619.html)
- Around 2026-09-23: flash purchasing managers' surveys (PMIs) for the eurozone and Germany. The German Ifo business survey usually comes out around the 21st to 24th. Both dates are typical, not confirmed.
- Ongoing: Brent crude around or above $100 and Middle East and Strait of Hormuz tensions. Any ceasefire or escalation has recently moved the DAX by several percent.
